what: Buying guaranteed output delivery without implementing GSZ
written: 2026-08-22. The first version was written before Protocols/Shamir.hpp had been read; that version and what reading it changed are both kept below.

the_idea.claim: GSZ's segmenting, player elimination and king exist to reach t < n/3. At t < n/4 a degree-2t sharing is directly correctable, so robustness can be the decoder that is already written rather than a new protocol.
the_idea.arithmetic: Reed-Solomon corrects e errors iff n - d >= 2e + 1. A product before degree reduction is d = 2t and robustness wants e = t, so n - 2t >= 2t + 1, i.e. n >= 4t + 1.

the_risk_that_was_written_down_and_then_.what_was_written: This assumes MP-SPDZ's Shamir multiplication publicly opens a degree-2t sharing. If instead each party re-shares its local product, the decode does not apply and the whole analysis changes. Protocols/Shamir.hpp gets read before anything gets run.
the_risk_that_was_written_down_and_then_.what_reading_found: Half wrong, and the half that was wrong is the half that was deployed.
the_risk_that_was_written_down_and_then_.plain_shamir: Protocols/Shamir.hpp is GRR re-sharing: prepare_mul does resharing->add_mine(x * y * rec_factor) for the first 2t+1 parties and finalize sums the received degree-t shares. There is NO degree-2t opening anywhere in the multiplication, so there is nothing for a decoder to correct. The n >= 4t+1 shortcut does not apply to malicious-shamir-party.x at all.
the_risk_that_was_written_down_and_then_.atlas: Protocols/Atlas.hpp is the Damgard-Nielsen shape and does exactly what the idea needs: get_double_sharing() returns {[r]_2t, [r]_t}, prepare() sends (x*y + r_2t) to a king, and exchange() has the king Lagrange-interpolate from 2t+1 shares and re-share the result at degree t.
the_risk_that_was_written_down_and_then_.so: The shortcut applies to ATLAS and not to Shamir. atlas-party.x ships in MP-SPDZ and is SEMI-HONEST; there is no malicious ATLAS.

what_is_already_in_the_engine.king_with_relays: ALREADY THERE. Atlas.hpp rotates the king round-robin: base_king, next_king = (next_king + 1) % P.num_players().
what_is_already_in_the_engine.segments_checkpoints_and_player_eliminat: Not there --- and the point of this note is that they may not be needed.

the_construction.step_2: e = xy + r is masked by a FRESH degree-2t random, so it is not secret. Open it to everyone instead of to a king.
the_construction.step_3: Each party decodes the n shares of e with Berlekamp-Welch, correcting up to T wrong ones and naming their senders, then computes [xy]_t = e - [r]_t entirely locally.
the_construction.what_this_removes: The king, whose word nobody now has to take; the re-sharing step; segments; checkpoints; player elimination.
the_construction.why_the_king_was_the_problem: ATLAS's king reconstructs from 2t+1 shares and then re-shares. A malicious king re-shares a consistent sharing of the WRONG value, and no amount of error correction on a consistent sharing catches that. This is exactly the 'consistent but wrong' case. Opening to everyone removes the party whose word was being taken.

predictions.quantity: elements per party per multiplication, online, n=9 T=2, no king, decode at every party
predictions.reasoning: each party sends its share of e to the other n-1 and there is no return leg, so the cost is n-1 = 8. ATLAS with a king is about 2 (one to the king, one back, amortised over the rotation).
predictions.against_the_deployed_baseline: about 1.0x the 8.000 that malicious-shamir-party.x spends online today. Malicious Shamir already pays for a sacrifice; this pays for the all-to-all instead and needs no sacrifice, because errors are corrected rather than detected.

predictions.reasoning: to the king and back becomes one all-to-all. If this lands, the robust protocol has FEWER rounds than the semi-honest one it is derived from.

predictions.quantity: global traffic against the n=7 abort-only baseline
predictions.reasoning: per-party about the same, times 9 parties instead of 7 = 1.29

predictions.predicted: one or two corrupted nodes are corrected AND named without the protocol stopping; three makes it refuse rather than guess
predictions.why_it_matters: this is the difference between rung 4 and rung 5, and naming without stopping has never been measured here

what_still_has_to_abort_and_why_that_is_.the_double_sharings: A malicious contributor can make [r]_t and [r]_2t inconsistent with each other, which no decode on either one alone catches. The check is a sacrifice: open a random combination and confirm the two degrees agree.
what_still_has_to_abort_and_why_that_is_.why_abort_is_fine_there: Preprocessing consumes no inputs. A failed offline run leaks nothing and denies nobody an outcome --- it is re-run, and a node that keeps failing it is removed between auctions, which is a governance action rather than a protocol one. Guaranteed output delivery is only needed once real inputs are in.
what_still_has_to_abort_and_why_that_is_.the_input_phase: Already robust here for a reason generic GSZ does not have: the dealer publishes a Pedersen commitment per share, so a node handed a bad share proves it to anybody by the commitment not opening. The complaint protocol a robust input phase normally needs is paid for by publicly auditable MPC.

what_this_does_not_buy: GSZ's asymptotics. GSZ is 5.5 to 7.5 with a king; this gives up the king and pays n-1.

A smaller consortium. n = 9 is two more institutions than n = 7, and POSITION.md's own risk register says the binding constraint is assembling the consortium at all. A governance cost, not a technical one.
Anything at T = 3 without going to n = 13.
the_alternative_that_looks_cheap_and_is_: Keeping n = 7 and dropping to T = 1 also satisfies n >= 4T+1 and costs no traffic. It also drops the privacy threshold to 1, so any two colluding nodes reconstruct every order in the book. Not available to a venue.
